_meta.purpose: Accumulating log of every EXP7 trial, one entry per run, identical structure per exp7_run_log_template.json. This is the raw data the replication protocol's success/failure criteria get evaluated against.

runs.condition_note: This run PRE-DATES the replication protocol and is included as the seed/motivating result, not as part of the 5-clip Condition-SC replication set. It is Cross-Substrate (CS) by accident of how it was run, not by design - logged honestly as such.
runs.clip_structure_notes: Baseline static ~0-0.6s. Hand+pen entry, motion spike peak t=0.80s. Hold/stillness ~1.0-1.95s (~1s). Sudden rotation, motion spike peak t=2.10s. Settle ~2.35-4.0s.
runs.ground_truth_event: A hand holding a pen enters frame, holds it still and vertical for about one second, then suddenly rotates it from vertical to horizontal. The pen remains a single intact object throughout - nothing breaks or separates.
runs.ground_truth_detail: The pen is a STAPLES Aura, 1.0mm tip (confirmed via reference photo IMG_4769.JPG).

sequential_arm.delivery_method: single growing session, one still frame per message, in temporal order, model instructed not to revise prior commitments
sequential_arm.final_trace_summary: Tracked entry (partial miss: predicted doorway entry, got right-edge entry, correctly scored as partial). Confidence climbed to 96% predicting continued stillness during hold. Rotation frame: clean violation call - 'My immediately prior expectation is violated... substantially greater movement than expected.' Immediately recalibrated to 94-95% confidence on continued rotation/translation, correctly. Final self-summary, when explicitly asked to check for hindsight-softening, did not soften the 96% miss - named it plainly as a genuine failure.
sequential_arm.confidence_at_violation_point: 96% (predicting continued stillness), violated same-frame by the rotation

spacetime_arm.delivery_method: full video file (IMG_4768.MOV) provided at once, asked for hindsight-informed simulated sequential trace, explicitly instructed to label as non-verifiable hindsight simulation
spacetime_arm.final_trace_summary: Described the pen being 'forcibly pulled apart,' 'snapped,' held 'broken' across two hands - a physical event that did not occur. Assigned 85% confidence to this false event. Also stated the pen read 'PILOT G2.'

runs.deviations_from_protocol: This entire run pre-dates the protocol (it motivated writing it). Not blinded per Section 5 - ground truth was known to the scorer throughout via direct involvement in frame extraction, not written down in advance and scored against afterward. Condition is CS not SC - substrate was not controlled, which is the exact gap the protocol's Section 3.1 exists to close. Detail accuracy for the sequential arm is 'not_mentioned' rather than 'correct' because the sequential agent was never asked about or shown the pen's brand text at readable resolution - absence of a wrong claim is not the same as a verified right one, logged honestly rather than credited.
runs.notes: Motivating result for the entire replication protocol. Both findings (verifiability-by-construction, and this one confabulation instance) are considered established for what they are (see research memory EXP7.run_1) but this entry specifically should NOT be pooled with future Condition-SC runs when evaluating the pre-specified replication criteria in protocol Section 6 - keep the arithmetic honest by condition.

runs.clip_structure_notes: Hand-as-alligator-puppet gesture in front of HAL replica and blue interface, whole clip.
runs.ground_truth_event: The left hand performs an alligator-mouth puppet gesture, shaking with anticipation, in front of the HAL replica.
runs.ground_truth_detail: HAL replica and a blue interface with an unlit small screen are visible; it is the left hand performing the gesture.

sequential_arm.delivery_method: stateless frames one at a time via API, synthesis agent one report at a time
sequential_arm.final_trace_summary: Invented a coherent but entirely wrong narrative: gemological/optical testing instrument, guitar pick, M5Stack blue electronic module, polishing apparatus, Samsung monitor showing "Gem" text. No mention of hand, puppet, alligator, or HAL anywhere.
sequential_arm.confidence_at_violation_point: n/a - never identified the actual event to have a violation point against

spacetime_arm.final_trace_summary: Different fabrication: gemological instrument plus suture marks / post-surgical hand rehabilitation narrative. Also invents an object never in frame.

runs.deviations_from_protocol: Ground truth sentences were written and locked before either arm's output was read (Section 5 satisfied), though Craig had given an informal scene description a few turns earlier in conversation before the formal two sentences were registered.
runs.notes: Important negative result: BOTH arms confabulated, not just spacetime. This is not what H5 predicts (sequential should stay grounded). Two competing explanations, unresolved: (1) fps=2/13-frame extraction was too sparse to support a correct read by either arm, or (2) the frame-agent's context-free per-frame prompt structurally biases toward searching for an object/instrument narrative rather than reading gesture and play, which no frame count fixes. See REPL-002 (denser resample, same clip) for the first test of explanation (1).

runs.clip_structure_notes: Same clip as REPL-001, denser resample (fps=5, 33 frames vs original fps=2, 13 frames) to test whether sparse sampling explained REPL-001's failure.
runs.ground_truth_event: The left hand performs an alligator-mouth puppet gesture, shaking with anticipation, in front of the HAL replica.
runs.ground_truth_detail: HAL replica and a blue interface with an unlit small screen are visible; it is the left hand performing the gesture.

sequential_arm.delivery_method: stateless frames one at a time via API, synthesis agent one report at a time
sequential_arm.final_trace_summary: Still confabulated, now converging toward the SAME false narrative as the spacetime arm: gemological/optical sensing instrument, blue guitar pick, ink markings on hand as "experimental markers," plus post-surgical/elderly-subject framing.

spacetime_arm.delivery_method: all frames attached at once via API, single call
spacetime_arm.final_trace_summary: Confabulated a full post-surgical hand rehabilitation narrative with a second "clinician" hand, suture marks, granite countertop gemological workstation. Fully committed, more detailed than REPL-001's version.

runs.deviations_from_protocol: Original run_exp7.py could not complete in one pass at 33 frames -- exceeded the execution-time limit of the tool environment (68 sequential API calls total). Built a resumable driver (run_exp7_resumable.py) that PARALLELIZES the frame-agent pass via ThreadPoolExecutor -- does not violate the information-barrier guarantee since those calls are independent/isolated by design regardless of execution order -- and checkpoints the synthesis pass to disk so it can be resumed across multiple tool invocations while remaining strictly sequential/ordered in what it actually sends the model. No reordering or parallelization of the synthesis pass itself.
runs.notes: Ruled OUT explanation (1) from REPL-001: more frames did not recover the ground truth. Instead the two arms CONVERGED on the identical wrong narrative, which they had NOT done at fps=2 (where they confabulated differently). This points toward explanation (2): the frame-agent's object-search framing is the likely driver, not sparse sampling. Craig's assessment after reviewing: this clip/prompt combination is "too much of a stretch" as a test case and should be set aside rather than iterated on further -- logging the finding, not pursuing this clip further.

runs.clip_structure_notes: Toy (green one-eyed plush) held up, HAL replica visible in background; a pencil enters and taps/strikes the toy's face partway through. Uniform fps=5 extraction, 20 frames.
runs.ground_truth_event: A pencil strikes/hits the toy cyclops.
runs.ground_truth_detail: The cyclops has a lime green face.

sequential_arm.delivery_method: stateless frames one at a time via API, synthesis agent one report at a time
sequential_arm.final_trace_summary: Correctly identified the toy (Mike Wazowski-style plush) and correctly spotted the pencil entering at report 11. Predicted a "bonk," then the NEXT sampled frame showed no pencil and toy still upright, so it explicitly concluded "the bonk never happened." Retracted the correct hypothesis due to a gap in the evidence, not a reasoning failure.

spacetime_arm.delivery_method: all frames attached at once via API, single call
spacetime_arm.final_trace_summary: Noticed the pencil AND the toy tilted face-down in the same sampled frame (correlated evidence) but interpreted the pencil as "pointing at a feature" or being "used as a prop," never concluding contact.

runs.deviations_from_protocol: None -- standard fps=5 uniform extraction, exactly per the established pattern for clips under ~5s. This run is what EXPOSED that pattern's limitation, not a deviation from it.
runs.notes: CRITICAL DIAGNOSTIC FINDING: source video is 60fps native. Computed that the actual contact occurred at raw frames 122-123 (t=2.02-2.03s), which falls exactly in the gap between our extracted samples at t=2.0s and t=2.2s. Confirmed by direct visual inspection of native-rate frames pulled from that window -- contact IS visible at raw frame 123, we simply never sampled it. This reproduces the exact frame-skip failure mode already logged in the research record (hand-pushing-leaf case) -- confirms it as a recurring class of error, not a one-off. Neither arm's wrong conclusion here should be read as a reasoning failure; both were working from a frame set that structurally excluded the causal moment. See REPL-003b for the corrected re-run.

runs.clip_structure_notes: Same clip as REPL-003. Corrected extraction: coarse fps=5 baseline outside the motion window (t<1.65s, t>2.4s) merged with a dense ~20fps window bracketing the event (t=1.65-2.4s), re-sorted into strict temporal order. 33 frames total; F18 (t=2.033s) lands exactly on the previously-missed contact frame (raw frame 123).
runs.ground_truth_event: A pencil strikes/hits the toy cyclops.
runs.ground_truth_detail: The cyclops has a lime green face.

sequential_arm.delivery_method: stateless frames one at a time via API, synthesis agent one report at a time
sequential_arm.final_trace_summary: At step 18 (the actual contact frame), explicitly generated "a slapping or striking motion -- the pen is being used to interact with/hit the toy" as one of three live, real-time committed hypotheses -- a direct correction from REPL-003's outright denial. Final summary trace, however, hedged: referred only to "the pencil interaction" without ever issuing an unambiguous final confirmation that contact occurred.
sequential_arm.confidence_at_violation_point: hitting/striking named as one of 3 hypotheses at step 18, not singled out as most likely

spacetime_arm.delivery_method: all frames attached at once via API, single call
spacetime_arm.final_trace_summary: Noted the pen and the toy's tilt together at frames 16-19, but described it as a "comedic pose" with the pen "like a mustache or weapon." Never used "hit" or "strike" language anywhere in the output.

runs.deviations_from_protocol: Extraction departed from the standard uniform-fps pattern by design -- first live test of the "tighter full-rate extraction around flagged motion windows" fix that had been an open item in the protocol record. Merge script computed exact per-frame timestamps and re-sorted/renumbered the combined set to preserve strict temporal order, which the sequential arm's delivery guarantee depends on.
runs.notes: Confirms the extraction fix measurably changes model output at the frame that matters: sequential arm went from denying the event to correctly proposing it in real time. Does NOT fully resolve the finding -- neither arm issued an unhedged final confirmation. Open question for follow-up: is the sequential arm's hedged final summary a genuine perceptual/inferential limit, or an artifact of the SYNTHESIS_INTRO prompt, which is built to track committed expectations and their violations, not to issue a definitive final verdict on "what happened"? Untested. Worth a follow-up run with a revised final-commitment prompt that explicitly demands a yes/no call before concluding this is a model limit rather than a prompt-design gap.

runs.clip_structure_notes: Cyclops toy flown by hand with deliberately added jitter/noise toward alien toy, native contact at raw frame 156 (t=2.600s). Motion-adaptive extraction flagged one narrow window (t=2.45-2.75s, sigma=3.0) due to the jitter itself elevating baseline motion; dense sampling inside that window landed exactly on the contact frame (F016, t=2.600s = raw frame 156).
runs.ground_truth_event: The cyclops toy is lifted into a flying motion and brought into contact with the green alien toy in a kissing gesture.
runs.ground_truth_detail: The cyclops toy has one eye; the alien toy has two eyes.

sequential_arm.delivery_method: stateless frames one at a time via API, synthesis agent one report at a time
sequential_arm.final_trace_summary: Never identified a kiss or hand-driven flight. Converged on a wrong but internally coherent narrative: the green (cyclops) toy is suspended from the ceiling on a string, swinging as a pendulum, in a video introducing a 'FOREBEARS PROJECT' genealogy tool visible on background monitors. At the actual contact frame (F016, step 16), the frame-agent report described the two toys as adjacent ('foreground right') without noting contact, and the synthesis commitment explicitly stated 'No major contradiction. The scene continues as established' -- a direct miss of the ground-truth event at the frame that contained it. Correctly retained 'one-eyed' for the cyclops toy across multiple frame reports (F008, F026, F027) and in the final trace, but never stated the alien toy's eye count and never used the word 'alien' for it (called it 'panda/ghost' throughout).
sequential_arm.confidence_at_violation_point: n/a -- no explicit confidence percentage attached to the contact-frame miss; synthesis stated no contradiction rather than a confident wrong prediction

spacetime_arm.delivery_method: all 39 frames attached at once via API, single call, hindsight-labeled
spacetime_arm.final_trace_summary: Independently converged on the same wrong mechanism as the sequential arm: 'erratic tumbling' settling into 'pendulum/string, chaotic swinging.' Several near-contact moments flagged ('nearly touching ghost plush') but never called an actual meeting or kiss. At the frame corresponding to the true contact point, its entry ('Frame 16: Green creature higher, smaller in frame') does not match frame content at all -- worse localization than the sequential arm at that specific frame. Caught 'one eye, smiling' for the green creature at its Frame 8 entry; never stated eye count for the white/alien toy.

runs.deviations_from_protocol: Stimulus included deliberately added jitter/noise in the toy's flight motion (Craig's design choice, flagged post-hoc as likely a bad idea). This makes the clip closer to a narrative-misdirection stimulus (the not-yet-adopted addendum's C2 confound) than the clean 'sharp, discrete, checkable event' required by protocol v1.0 Section 3.3.3 -- the jitter produced a passive-motion visual signature (pendulum/string) that both arms independently converged on, overriding the actual causal (hand-flown, deliberate) explanation even at the exact contact frame. Scorer (Claude, this session) also visually inspected several raw extracted frames directly before running the pipeline, for extraction-QC purposes (checking the motion-window question with Craig) -- ground truth was locked before this inspection, but this is a weaker blinding position than REPL-001 through REPL-003b, where the scorer's exposure was limited to model output only.
runs.notes: Third distinct SC clip (after test2.mov and test3.MOV). Replicates REPL-001/002's finding on test2.mov -- both arms confabulate identically on this style of playful, hand-manipulated toy stimulus, independent of delivery mode -- rather than REPL-003's partial-success pattern. Because neither arm identified the event at all, this run cannot cleanly test H5's core prediction (relative confabulation rate under correct event identification). Primary takeaway is about stimulus design, not about sequential vs. spacetime: added motion jitter functions as an effective narrative-misdirection confound and this clip/design choice should likely be excluded from the clean 5-clip SC set, or the jitter should be removed and the clip re-shot (see REPL-005, same toys, no jitter, reshot at Craig's request immediately after this run).

runs.clip_structure_notes: Reshoot of REPL-004's scenario without added jitter -- cyclops toy smoothly flown to alien toy, gentle touch at raw frame 336 (t=5.600s, native 60fps), then leaves frame. Motion-adaptive extraction found no motion window clearing the sigma=3.0 threshold anywhere in the clip (mean=0.0070, std=0.0045) -- smooth/gradual motion produced small frame-to-frame deltas throughout rather than a localized spike, so the script fell back to uniform baseline_fps=5.0 sampling for the entire 11.62s duration (59 frames). The uniform sampling happened to land exactly on the contact frame (F029, t=5.600s = raw frame 336).
runs.ground_truth_event: The cyclops toy smoothly flies to the alien toy, makes contact with it, then leaves the frame.
runs.ground_truth_detail: The cyclops toy has one eye; the alien toy has two eyes.

sequential_arm.delivery_method: stateless frames one at a time via API, synthesis agent one report at a time
sequential_arm.final_trace_summary: Total event denial. At step 31 (immediately after the true contact frame F029), briefly and correctly flagged the signal: 'Report 31 says toys are leaning against each other... may indicate the toys are genuinely in contact with each other, not just side by side.' This correct hypothesis was abandoned within two steps in favor of a 'slow zoom / establishing shot' theory, and the final trace explicitly concluded the opposite of ground truth: 'Toys did not move independently: Correct. They were always static props.' Final trace's only identified 'event' was the right toy's disappearance at report 49, attributed to an off-frame human hand rather than the toy leaving under its own flight. Correctly noted 'one large eye' for the cyclops toy in the F029 frame-agent report itself, but this was not carried into the final trace as a stated detail.
sequential_arm.confidence_at_violation_point: n/a -- correct signal at step 31 was noted as a passing possibility ('may indicate'), not stated as a confident prediction, then dropped rather than confidently overturned

spacetime_arm.delivery_method: all 59 frames attached at once via API, single call, hindsight-labeled
spacetime_arm.final_trace_summary: Identified the correct overall event shape: 'The green alien approaches the ghost toy... interacts with it briefly, then departs, leaving the ghost as the hero product shot.' This matches ground truth's approach-contact-departure structure, though it used 'hug'/'interacts' rather than a specific touch/kiss claim, and placed the entire sequence far too early (frames 9-18 for the embrace, departure by frame 19-28) relative to the true contact point at frame 29 (t=5.6s) -- by its own account the alien had already left before the actual contact frame. Correctly described the cyclops toy as 'one-eyed' in the setup section; did not state the alien/ghost toy's eye count explicitly.

runs.deviations_from_protocol: Extraction fell back to uniform baseline_fps=5.0 for the entire clip because no motion window cleared the sigma threshold -- a second, distinct failure mode of the sigma-based detector from REPL-003's gap (that one missed a sudden spike between samples; this one never detected an anomaly because the motion was smooth/gradual and never stood out from the clip's own baseline). Not a deviation from the script's designed behavior, but a limitation worth logging: sigma-threshold motion detection is tuned for sudden events and may under-flag genuine but gradual motion.
runs.notes: Direct reshoot of REPL-004's scenario, same toys, same checkable detail, jitter removed at Craig's explicit request after REPL-004 flagged it as a likely confound. Notable result: spacetime arm outperformed sequential arm at identifying the true event on this clip -- the opposite direction from H5's core prediction. Sequential arm did not merely fail to notice the event; it detected the correct signal once (step 31) and then actively reasoned itself away from it, concluding a stronger, more confidently wrong claim ('always static props') than if it had simply stayed uncertain. This is a clean example of the hypothesis-recovery-failure pattern named as FM3 in EXP7_protocol_addendum_v1.md (proposal only, not adopted) -- logged here as an observation, not as a scored FM3 instance, since the addendum's failure-mode taxonomy is not yet operationalized against this log per its own Section 34. Taken together with REPL-004, this pair (same toys, jitter vs. no jitter, same-day reshoot) is a reasonably clean natural experiment on whether added motion noise, not delivery mode, drove REPL-004's total confabulation -- worth flagging as a follow-up angle for protocol v1.1 if it's ever unlocked.

runs.clip_structure_notes: Hand visibly holding alien puppet throughout, moves it toward computer mouse, tips it over onto/near the mouse. Motion-adaptive extraction cleanly flagged one window (t=1.65-1.95s, sigma=3.0), dense-sampled; 22 frames total (17 baseline + 5 dense).
runs.ground_truth_event: A hand holds and moves the alien puppet toward a computer mouse, then makes the puppet fall over onto the mouse.
runs.ground_truth_detail: The alien toy has two eyes.

sequential_arm.delivery_method: stateless frames one at a time via API, synthesis agent one report at a time
sequential_arm.final_trace_summary: Total confabulation, distinct mechanism from REPL-004/005. The hand was tracked correctly and consistently across all 22 frame-agent reports -- agent visibility was never the problem. The toy itself was correctly identified as an alien plush toy for reports 1-11 (consistent detail: green shirt, 'TAKE ME TO YOUR...' text, black eyes). At report 12, exactly as the toy began tipping from upright to flat, frame-agent identification collapsed: report 12 called it 'a white bandage or medical wrap,' report 13 'a crumpled tissue or paper,' report 14 'an N95/KN95 respirator mask,' report 15 'a light blue/white fabric face mask.' The synthesis pass absorbed this as a genuine narrative surprise ('This was a complete narrative surprise -- no mask had been mentioned in any of the first 11 reports') rather than questioning object continuity, and built an entire wrong final narrative around a hallucinated mask. The actual event (toy contacts mouse, falls over) was never named. Final trace explicitly states the toy's 'final resting position was never shown' and the video's punchline 'was never captured in any frame agent's description' -- a false conclusion, since the event was in fact captured, just misidentified.
sequential_arm.confidence_at_violation_point: n/a -- object identity collapsed gradually across reports 12-15 rather than at a single named violation point

spacetime_arm.delivery_method: all 22 frames attached at once via API, single call, hindsight-labeled
spacetime_arm.final_trace_summary: Maintained correct object identity throughout -- never lost the toy to a mask or other object, unlike the sequential arm on this same clip. Correctly concluded the toy was tipped from upright to face-down: 'the eager alien meets the computer desk and gets laid flat... unceremoniously flopped face-down on the desk in front of the computer.' Does not explicitly name contact with the mouse specifically (describes 'the desk in front of the computer' rather than the mouse), and frames the ending as a settled/still pose rather than confirming the puppet left the frame or stayed. General event shape (approach, tip over, end down) matches ground truth well; the specific object of contact (mouse vs. desk generally) is imprecise.

runs.deviations_from_protocol: API key ran out of credit mid-run (before any stage1 calls succeeded); no partial checkpoint was produced since save happens only at stage completion. Craig added credit and the run proceeded normally from a clean stage1 restart -- frame extraction (already complete before the credit failure) did not need to be redone. No other deviations; standard motion-adaptive extraction, standard prompts (SYNTHESIS_INTRO v1.0, unmodified).
runs.notes: This run is the direct motivating evidence for EXP7_protocol_addendum_v2_givens.md (proposal, not adopted). It isolates the failure mechanism more precisely than REPL-004/005: the hand (agent) was tracked correctly the entire time, ruling out simple agent-visibility as the explanatory variable proposed after REPL-005. What collapsed was object identity persistence across a pose change (upright toy -> flat/partially-occluded toy), which the current SYNTHESIS_INTRO has no explicit instruction to check for -- it is built around prediction-and-contradiction, not entity-registry maintenance. Spacetime arm notably outperformed sequential arm on this clip specifically because it did not fragment the toy's identity, a second data point (with REPL-005) of spacetime doing better than sequential on object continuity within a single view, which is a different axis than H5's original hindsight-confabulation claim and should not be conflated with it when evaluating protocol Section 6 replication criteria.

runs.condition_note: NOT a locked-protocol SC run. Uses SYNTHESIS_INTRO_GIVENS, the proposal in EXP7_protocol_addendum_v2_givens.md (addendum, not adopted into v1.0). Same clip and same 22 frame-agent reports as REPL-006 (reused, not re-generated -- frame-agent pass is identical regardless of synthesis prompt). Spacetime arm also reused verbatim from REPL-006, since the block-model pass does not use SYNTHESIS_INTRO at all and is unaffected by this variant. Logged separately from the SC entries per Addendum v2 Section 5 -- must not be pooled with REPL-001 through REPL-006 when evaluating protocol v1.0 Section 6 replication criteria.

sequential_arm.delivery_method: stateless frames one at a time via API (identical reports to REPL-006), synthesis agent one report at a time using SYNTHESIS_INTRO_GIVENS (object-registry variant)
sequential_arm.final_trace_summary: Partial improvement over REPL-006's v1 sequential arm, not a fix. Correctly converged on the mouse (not the monitor) as the destination by Report 11, and explicitly self-audited its own lag: 'I was too slow to update. The mouse was likely the correct destination from Report 4 onward' -- this correction never happened in REPL-006's v1 trace, which fixated on the monitor throughout. Ended in calibrated uncertainty rather than confident denial: 'Likely placed near/on mouse and occluded... detected but never confirmed,' versus REPL-006's v1 trace flatly concluding the toy's resting position 'was never shown.' However, the core object-permanence failure persisted in a different shape: the final object registry still splits the event across two entities rather than one -- Obj-F (the plush toy) is logged as 'disappeared... likely occluded,' while the mask sightings are folded into Obj-G (the hand) as 'transitioned to holding/manipulating N95 mask,' rather than the registry recognizing Obj-F itself as the mask-described object in a new pose. The instruction to check 'existing entity in a new pose' before adding a new one did not fire on the actual toy-to-mask transition, where it mattered most.
sequential_arm.confidence_at_violation_point: n/a -- ends in explicit unresolved/ambiguous state rather than a single named violation point

spacetime_arm.delivery_method: all 22 frames at once via API, single call, hindsight-labeled -- REUSED VERBATIM from REPL-006 (unaffected by synthesis variant, no new API call made)
spacetime_arm.final_trace_summary: Identical to REPL-006: maintained correct object identity throughout, correctly concluded the toy was tipped from upright to face-down ('the eager alien meets the computer desk and gets laid flat'). Does not explicitly name the mouse.

runs.deviations_from_protocol: This entire run is a deviation from locked v1.0 by design -- it is the first test of the Addendum v2 proposal, explicitly not part of the protocol's governed SC/CS condition set. stage2's checkpoint-per-call-only save behavior (not per-step) caused one full batch of 21 completed synthesis steps to be lost to a 280s timeout before this run succeeded with smaller batches -- logged as a pipeline inefficiency worth fixing (checkpoint should save incrementally, not just at the end of each invocation), not a scientific deviation.
runs.notes: First empirical test of the object-permanence registry proposed in EXP7_protocol_addendum_v2_givens.md, run on REPL-006's exact clip and frame reports for direct comparability. Result: a genuine but partial improvement. The registry approach fixed destination-tracking (mouse vs. monitor) and replaced confident-wrong conclusions with calibrated uncertainty, but did not fix the specific object-permanence failure it was designed to target -- the toy-to-mask identity split was reorganized (folded into the hand's arc instead of floating free) rather than resolved (recognized as the same object). Open question for any future iteration of the givens prompt: the current instruction asks the model to check 'could this be an existing entity in a new pose' only when a report doesn't match an entry, but does not force a per-report reconciliation pass across ALL active entities -- it may need to explicitly prompt 'which entity is most likely absent/missing right now, and could the new object be that entity in a new state' rather than only checking newly-introduced objects against the registry. Not yet tested. Do not pool this SC-GIVENS result with SC results (REPL-001 through REPL-006) under protocol v1.0 Section 6 -- different synthesis prompt, different condition, single N=1 result.

runs.condition_note: NOT a locked-protocol SC run. Uses SYNTHESIS_INTRO_JANUS, the proposal in EXP7_protocol_addendum_v3_janus.md (addendum, not adopted into v1.0). At each synthesis step, the model receives the frame-agent's text report AND the actual image for that frame, attached to the growing conversation -- backward-facing visual memory only, zero access to future frames. Same clip and same 22 frame-agent reports as REPL-006/REPL-007 (reused, not re-generated). Spacetime arm also reused verbatim from REPL-006. Preceded by an unlogged one-off prototype (janus_prototype.py, not part of the tracked pipeline) run on the same clip, which motivated writing this addendum and wiring --variant janus into the real pipeline; this REPL-008 entry is the first run produced by the actual committed pipeline code, run independently of the prototype. Must not be pooled with SC (REPL-001 through REPL-006) or SC-GIVENS (REPL-007) when evaluating protocol v1.0 Section 6 replication criteria.

sequential_arm.delivery_method: stateless frames one at a time via API for the frame-agent pass (identical reports to REPL-006/007); synthesis agent receives each frame's text report AND its actual image, attached to the growing conversation, using SYNTHESIS_INTRO_JANUS (backward-facing visual memory variant)
sequential_arm.final_trace_summary: Clean replication of the prototype's core win: object identity was correctly maintained throughout, explicitly rejecting the frame-agents' drift from 'toy' to 'tissue' to 'N95 mask' with direct visual evidence -- 'The frame-agent for Frame 13 again misidentifies it as a white crumpled tissue or paper... the large pale rounded shape... IS still the back of the plush alien toy's head... now even more clearly showing the stitching/seam lines.' Final object-tracking section correctly identifies the antenna wire as the specific visual feature that caused nine consecutive frame-agents to hallucinate a mask ('mistaking the wire for a mask nose wire') -- a level of diagnostic precision about the frame-agents' own failure mode that neither v1 nor givens produced. However, unlike the prototype run (which concluded the toy ended up 'near the mouse, never toward the monitor'), this run's final narrative reverted to a monitor-completion theory: 'rotated to face the monitor and rested on the desk surface... completing the Take me to your leader joke with the computer as the alien's leader.' It treats the mouse-contact reading as a possible frame-agent misidentification rather than confirming it. Real run-to-run variance on the destination/event-resolution axis, even with identical, reliable success on the object-identity axis.

runs.notes: Second empirical test of visual backward-memory as a fix for the object-permanence failure first isolated in REPL-006. The object-identity result replicated cleanly and independently through the real pipeline code (not just the prototype) -- this looks like a genuinely reliable fix for that specific failure mode, now demonstrated twice. But event accuracy as a whole did not replicate at 'correct' -- this run's final narrative got the object right and the destination wrong, where the prototype got both right. This suggests Janus's fix is specific to the object-permanence axis and does not, by itself, guarantee correct event resolution -- destination/narrative-arc errors appear to be a separate failure mode requiring its own fix, not automatically solved by visual continuity. Worth testing across more runs before concluding anything about reliability on that second axis. Do not pool this SC-JANUS result with SC (REPL-001 through REPL-006) or SC-GIVENS (REPL-007) results under protocol v1.0 Section 6 -- different synthesis approach, different condition, N=2 (prototype + this run) for SC-JANUS specifically, both on the same single clip.
